description: What the Preferences window may use: showing itself once its page is styled, being dragged by its top bar, and Tauri's core defaults, which let it tell the app whether the Dock icon rotates. It has no file permissions at all: settings live in the app's local storage. The app's own commands are granted one by one (build.rs lists them all), those its code calls and no others, as src/command-permissions.node.test.ts checks: the command line, the default app, whether there is a Quick Look preview to turn off and the settings that turn it off, the list of agents and detecting them, updating an agent, signing it in and stopping either (each a fixed command of the agent's own, for an agent the window names and nothing more), looking at this Mac's Tailscale and whether a Gateway answers at an address (the probe sends nothing), (read only: whether it is installed, signed in and sees other computers), opening its app or its download page, connecting and disconnecting an OpenClaw connection to its Gateway and asking where it is (the window gives only the connection's name and the setup code the person pasted), adding, changing and removing an OpenClaw connection (adding or widening one is a question of the system's, and no secret is ever returned), installing the Redlines skill in the folder an agent reads skills from and looking at what is there (the app's own text, for an agent the window names and nothing more), the appearance and the zoom, and asking for the default folder of new documents (the window is shown a folder panel, and given no right to use what it picks). Adding or removing an agent, updating one, signing one in and installing a skill are this window's alone.
